note: Draft feature definitions for capabilities NOT yet in openapi.json. Each draft feature defines schema structure and overlay into the spec so draft fields appear in the tree, validate (typed), and feed the prompt/coverage — each flagged 'draft'. Remove a feature entry once it lands in the real openapi.json. Enrichment and rules are in qa-studio/enrichment/ and qa-studio/rules/ respectively, prefixed with the feature name (e.g., jobs.split.can_be_split.json).

features.title: Split Order / Split Jobs Across Vehicles
features.description: Allow large jobs to be split across multiple vehicles when a single vehicle lacks sufficient capacity. Split orders apply to jobs only (not shipments). Each split portion retains the original job ID and is tagged with a split_indicator in the response route steps.

split.description: Split Order configuration (DRAFT, not in spec): enable splitting a large job across multiple vehicles.

can_be_split.description: Whether this job may be split across multiple vehicles. Default: false. If false and job demand exceeds single-vehicle capacity, the job becomes unassigned.

max_splits.description: Maximum number of vehicles this job can be split across. Required if can_be_split=true. Each split sub-job receives a split_indicator in response (0 to max_splits-1).

quant.description: Minimum quantity each split must carry, as a ratio of the original job load (0.0 to 1.0). Applies only when problem.objective.load_dimension=1; multi-dimension behavior is TBC. Optional.

constraints: Split applies to jobs.items only; shipments do not support split.
If can_be_split=true, max_splits must be present and ≥ 1.
quant applies only when problem.objective.load_dimension=1; multi-dimension semantics undefined (mark TBC).
Sub-jobs created by a split share the same job ID as the original.
Each split sub-job carries split_indicator (0-based) and per-split pickup/delivery arrays in response route steps.

routes.steps.split_indicator.description: 0-based indicator identifying which split portion this step represents. Only present for split jobs. Range: 0 to (job.split.max_splits - 1).
routes.steps.split_indicator.note: Informational only; not validated in request. Present in response only if split job.

routes.steps.pickup.description: Sub-volume(s) of the original job's pickup load carried in this split. Sum of all split portions' pickup arrays equals the original job's pickup.
routes.steps.pickup.note: Informational only; reflects the split allocation computed by the solver.

routes.steps.delivery.description: Sub-volume(s) of the original job's delivery load carried in this split. Sum of all split portions' delivery arrays equals the original job's delivery.
routes.steps.delivery.note: Informational only; reflects the split allocation computed by the solver.

testingSuggestions: Negative-validation: Malformed split input (wrong types, split on a shipment) → expect HTTP 400 validation error.
Positive: High delivery volume (e.g. 5x vehicle capacity) with can_be_split=false or absent → expect job in result.unassigned.
Positive: Same high-volume job with can_be_split=true, max_splits sufficient, and enough vehicles → expect valid split solution where sub-deliveries sum to the original.
Boundary: max_splits exactly equal to the minimum number of vehicles needed; quant at the minimum feasible ratio.
Interaction: Multi-dimension load (load_dimension > 1) with quant set → test whether error or silently ignored (TBC).
limitations: Jobs only — shipments are not supported.
quant multi-dimension behavior is undefined in the source specification (mark TBC for future clarification).

features.source: Unassigned Reasons for Vehicles Understanding Doc.pdf
features.title: Explain Why Idle Vehicles Are Left Unused
features.description: Add vehicle-side diagnostics explaining why idle vehicles weren't used when unassigned work exists. This is the vehicle-side dual of result.unassigned[].reason. Distinguishes hard capability limits (impossible to serve) from cost/objective decisions (could serve, but too expensive).

report_unused_vehicle_reason.description: When true, populate result.unused_vehicles[] for idle vehicles whenever the solution has unassigned tasks. Flexible API only; Fast engine silently ignores.

result.unused_vehicles.description: Present only when report_unused_vehicle_reason=true AND result.unassigned[] is non-empty. Array of idle (empty-route) vehicles with explanations for why they were not used.
result.unused_vehicles.note: Absent if no unassigned tasks exist (even if vehicles are idle). Present but empty [] if unassigned tasks exist but all vehicles are used.

result.unused_vehicles.reasons.description: Distinct hard-constraint reasons aggregated across all unassigned units this vehicle cannot serve. Empty if vehicle can feasibly serve every unassigned unit.

result.unused_vehicles.feasible_unassign.description: true if vehicle could serve at least one unassigned unit on its empty route (marks cost/objective decision, not capability limit). false if vehicle is incapable of serving any unassigned unit (hard constraint blocks all of them).

constraints: Only emitted when report_unused_vehicle_reason=true and result.unassigned[] is non-empty.
Only reports completely idle (empty-route) vehicles; partially used vehicles with spare capacity are never reported.
Feasibility check is standalone per-unit; does not consider whether combination of units would be jointly feasible.
reasons are deduplicated and aggregated per vehicle, not linked to specific task IDs. Cross-reference each unassigned task's own reason to map specific task-constraint pairs.
Flexible API only; Fast engine (jsprit) silently ignores the option and never emits unused_vehicles.

Interaction with Split Orders: splitting phase runs before this diagnostic. An idle vehicle that could only carry a fragment of a splittable job still reports insufficient capacity / feasible_unassigned: false.

Re-optimization: report_unused_vehicle_reason is a request-level option. Each re-optimization computes idle/unassigned sets from that run's own solution; previous results never feed the diagnostic directly.

interpretationMatrix.interpretation: Vehicle is incapable of every unassigned unit; the listed constraints explain why. Hard capability limit.
Vehicle is blocked from some units (listed) but could serve at least one other — that one was left unassigned by cost/objective decision, not capability.
Vehicle could serve every unassigned unit; all were left unassigned by cost/objective. Investigate tuning, not capability.
Not emitted — only occurs when there were no unassigned units (feature definition gate).

testingSuggestions: Positive: Flag off (regression): Existing flexible suite with option unset — unused_vehicles must be absent, no solution diffs.
Positive: Incapable vehicle: Idle vehicle blocked by hard constraints, feasible_unassigned: false, reasons populated.
Positive: Feasible but not selected: Lowered unassigned_count_penalty causes cost decision, feasible_unassigned: true.
Positive: All-feasible idle vehicle: Could serve every unassigned unit, reasons: [], feasible_unassigned: true.
Positive: No idle vehicles: Unassigned tasks exist but all vehicles used, unused_vehicles: [] (present but empty).
Positive: No unassigned tasks: Flag on, full assignment, unused_vehicles absent (not present).
Positive: Shipment unit: Unassigned atomic shipments; capacity block on pickup yields one insufficient capacity reason for the whole shipment.
Positive: Time-window block: Idle vehicle whose time_window cannot reach any unassigned task → time_window requirements reason.
Positive: Zone / max_distance / max_travel_time blocks: Verify each maps to matching reason.
Positive: Mixed aggregate: Idle vehicle blocked from some units by skills and from others by capacity → both reasons present, deduplicated.
Negative-validation: Non-boolean report_unused_vehicle_reason → HTTP 400 Bad Request.
Positive: Fast engine: report_unused_vehicle_reason=true on jsprit → ignored, no unused_vehicles in response, no error.
Positive: Re-optimization: Flag carried through each optimization call; idle/unassigned sets recomputed from new solution.
Interaction: Split Orders: Splittable job remains unassigned after split phase → idle vehicle evaluated at full job demand, not fragments.
limitations: Flexible API only. Fast engine (jsprit) silently ignores report_unused_vehicle_reason.
Empty-route vehicles only. A vehicle used but with spare capacity for an unassigned task is NOT reported — only fully idle vehicles appear in unused_vehicles[].
Standalone per-unit feasibility. The check evaluates each unassigned unit independently on an empty route. Does not detect cases where a combination of units would be jointly infeasible.

Aggregated per vehicle. reasons is deduplicated and not linked to specific task IDs. To find which task hit which constraint, cross-reference each unassigned task's own reason with the vehicle's list.

Feasibility, not insertion order. feasible_unassigned reflects hard-constraint feasibility on an empty route. Under heuristic search a feasible unit may, rarely, be missed even under the default objective; treat feasible_unassigned: true as 'capability exists', not 'solver bug'.
Reason quality inherits unassigned caveats. Under a unified objective the exact reasons strings may degrade the same way unassigned[].reason does, but feasible_unassigned remains reliable.

features.title: One-to-Many Delivery Shipment
features.description: Allow a single pickup to distribute its load to multiple delivery locations as one logical shipment. Enables efficient modeling of warehouse distribution scenarios. Alternative to creating multiple shipments that share a pickup. All deliveries are jointly assigned or unassigned together.

deliveries.description: Array of delivery locations for a single pickup (ONE-TO-MANY). Must contain at least 2 deliveries. Mutually exclusive with singular delivery field.

items.description: Individual delivery in a one-to-many shipment.

id.description: Unique identifier for this delivery. Must be unique across all shipment steps (including pickup ID).

location_index.description: Index into the locations[] array. Identifies the delivery location.

amount.description: Delivery amount per dimension. Sum of all delivery amounts must equal shipment.amount dimension-by-dimension.

service.description: Service duration at this delivery location in seconds. Optional.

time_window.description: Time window [start, end] in seconds since epoch. Optional. Evaluated per delivery.

constraints: Exactly one of delivery or deliveries must be present; never both, never neither. Returns HTTP 400 if violated.
deliveries must contain at least 2 items (minimum array size). Single-delivery shipments use the singular delivery field.
SUM(deliveries[].amount) must equal shipment.amount, checked dimension-by-dimension. Returns HTTP 400 if sum mismatch.
All delivery IDs must be unique across the entire shipment (pickup + all deliveries). Returns HTTP 400 if duplicate.
Pickup and delivery IDs must not collide. Returns HTTP 400 if pickup ID equals any delivery ID.
Joint assignment: if any delivery becomes infeasible (capacity, time window, constraint), the entire shipment (pickup + all deliveries) is UNASSIGNED. No partial delivery is possible.
No partial fulfillment: each delivery is atomic. It must deliver 100% of its amount or be unassigned entirely.
All activities in a one-to-many shipment are assigned to the same vehicle. Cannot be split across multiple vehicles.
Delivery order is determined by the solver subject to sequence_order, time_windows, and follow_lifo_order constraints. Input array order is not preserved.
Compartments are NOT supported with deliveries (Stage 1 limitation). Returns HTTP 400 if both compartments and deliveries are present.
Shipment-level constraints (skills, zones, priority, etc.) apply to the entire shipment and cannot be overridden per delivery.
Relations (pinned assignments) do not yet support one-to-many shipments. Referencing a delivery ID in relations.steps returns HTTP 400.
Re-optimization does not yet support shipment_changes.modify/add/remove for one-to-many shipments.

result.routes[].steps[].id.description: Each pickup and each delivery appears as a separate step in the route. Pickup occurs once; deliveries follow.

result.routes[].steps[].type.description: Step type: 'pickup' for the shipment pickup, 'delivery' for each delivery.
result.routes[].steps[].type.note: No new step type introduced; deliveries use type: 'delivery' as before.

result.routes[].steps[].load.description: Vehicle load after this step. Increases at pickup, decreases at each delivery. Final load is 0 after last delivery.

result.routes[].steps[].distance.description: Distance from previous step to this step in meters.

result.routes[].steps[].duration.description: Duration from previous step to this step in seconds (travel + service).

result.routes[].steps[].arrival.description: Arrival time at this step in seconds since epoch.

testingSuggestions: Positive: Basic 1 pickup + 2 deliveries with correct amount sum (100+80=180 total).
Positive: 1 pickup + 3 deliveries, different locations, all deliveries after pickup.
Positive: Verify final vehicle load = 0 after all deliveries.
Positive: Verify load progression: start 0 → pickup +180 → D1 -100 → D2 -80 → end 0.
Positive: Multiple deliveries at same location (allowed, treated as separate steps).
Positive: Multi-dimensional amounts: amount=[300, 15], deliveries sum to [300, 15] per dimension.
Positive: All activities on same vehicle (joint assignment verified).
Negative-validation: Both delivery and deliveries provided → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Neither delivery nor deliveries provided → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: deliveries=[] (empty array) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: deliveries with 1 item (min=2) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Duplicate delivery IDs → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Pickup ID matches delivery ID → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Amount sum mismatch (100+80=180 but shipment amount=300) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Wrong amount dimensionality (delivery has 2 dims but shipment has 1) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Missing delivery ID → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Missing delivery amount → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Compartments + deliveries both present → HTTP 400.
Negative-infeasible: Vehicle capacity insufficient for pickup amount → entire shipment UNASSIGNED (not just pickup, not just one delivery).
Negative-infeasible: Time window violation on delivery 1 → entire shipment UNASSIGNED.
Negative-infeasible: max_time_in_vehicle violated for delivery 3 → entire shipment UNASSIGNED.
Boundary: Vehicle capacity exactly equals shipment amount → assigned successfully.
Boundary: Vehicle capacity exactly equals largest single delivery (not total) → depends on solver; expect infeasible.
Interaction: follow_lifo_order=true with multiple shipments → deliveries respect LIFO relative to other shipments.
Interaction: time_window on pickup and on deliveries → all must be satisfied.
Interaction: Skills required on shipment → pickup and all deliveries inherit; cannot override per delivery.
Interaction: Zones on shipment → all activities must be in permitted zones.
Backward compatibility: Existing 1-to-1 shipments (singular delivery) must pass regression suite unchanged.
limitations: Compartments NOT supported. If both compartments and deliveries are present, returns HTTP 400.
Relations (pinned assignments) do not yet support delivery groups. Attempting to reference a delivery ID in relations.steps returns HTTP 400.
Re-optimization does not yet support one-to-many shipments in shipment_changes. Modify/add/remove will return an error or silently ignore.
Delivery order is solver-determined; input array order is not preserved. Do not write tests expecting specific delivery order unless sequence_order or time_windows force it.
max_time_in_vehicle is evaluated per-delivery independently but triggers joint unassignment if any delivery violates it.

features.title: Coordinated Multi-Technician Jobs
features.description: Assign multiple technicians (jobs) to the same location with synchronized arrival within a specified tolerance. Each technician has their own vehicle, skills, service duration, availability, and load. Core guarantee: N technicians arrive within tolerance or entire group is unassigned (all-or-nothing). Uses different vehicles, joins skills at the group + member level, supports both last_arrival (default) and first_arrival service-start rules.

id.description: Unique group identifier. Must be globally unique across jobs, shipments, groups, and member IDs.

location_index.description: Index into locations[] array. All members of this group must service this single location.

skills.description: Group-level skills required by all members. Each member's vehicle must have (group skills UNION member skills). Optional.

service.description: Default service duration (seconds) for members who don't specify their own. Overridden by member-level service. Optional.

setup.description: Setup duration (seconds) before service begins. Applied before service starts. Optional; default 0.

time_windows.description: Default time windows [start, end] in seconds since epoch. Each member's time_windows overrides this entirely (not intersection). Optional.

arrival_sync_tolerance_seconds.description: Maximum allowed spread (latest arrival - earliest arrival) for members of this group, in seconds. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Max: 86400 (1 day).

service_start_rule.description: When synchronized arrival starts service. 'last_arrival' (default): all start service at latest arrival. 'first_arrival': each starts on own arrival.

jobs.description: Member technicians in this group. Minimum 2 members required. Each is a distinct technician with own ID.

items.description: A member technician (job) within a coordination group.

id.description: Unique member (technician) ID. Must be unique globally.

skills.description: Member-specific skills. Vehicle must have (group skills UNION member skills). Optional.

service.description: Member-specific service duration (seconds). Overrides group service. Optional.

setup.description: Member-specific setup duration (seconds). Overrides group setup. Optional; default 0.

time_windows.description: Member-specific time windows. Fully replaces group time_windows. Optional.

pickup.description: Pickup load for this member per dimension. Independent; affects member's vehicle capacity only. Optional.

delivery.description: Delivery load for this member per dimension. Independent; affects member's vehicle capacity only. Optional.

constraints: Flexible API only. Fast API (jsprit) returns HTTP 400 if coordinate_jobs is present.
Group IDs and all member IDs must be globally unique across jobs, shipments, shipment steps, and other group/member IDs. Returns HTTP 400 on collision.
Minimum 2 members per group required. Single-member groups return HTTP 400.
All members of a group must be assigned to different vehicles. If only one vehicle satisfies all skills, entire group → UNASSIGNED. Returns HTTP 400 if duplicate vehicles pinned to members.
All members must service the same location (group location_index). This is enforced; cannot be overridden per member.
Time windows: member time_windows fully replaces group time_windows (not intersection). If member omits time_windows, group default applies.
Skills union: vehicle must have (group skills UNION member skills) to be eligible for that member.
Service timing: under last_arrival (default), all members start service at max(arrival_times). Under first_arrival, each starts on own arrival.
Setup applies before service: arrival → (wait until sync instant) → setup → service → departure.
Loads are per-member, independent. Each member's load affects only its own vehicle's capacity. No group-level load.
All-or-nothing: if any member is infeasible (skills, capacity, time window, arrival tolerance violated), entire group → UNASSIGNED. No partial assignment.
Arrival synchronization: abs(serviceStart_A - serviceStart_B) <= arrival_sync_tolerance_seconds (after accounting for wait time). Raw arrivals need not satisfy tolerance.
Pinned technician: use relations with type=pinned, vehicle=<vehicle_id>, steps=[{type=job, id=<member_id>}] to force member to specific vehicle.
Cannot pin same vehicle to multiple members in the same group. Returns HTTP 400.
Cannot pin same member twice. Returns HTTP 400.
Member referenced in non-pinned relation returns HTTP 400.
Group referenced in any relation returns HTTP 400.
Re-optimization: job_changes.add/modify referencing member or group ID → rejected. job_changes.remove with group ID or all member IDs → removes entire group. Partial removal → HTTP 400.
shipment_changes not guarded (by design); coordinate members occupy same ID namespace as ordinary jobs; shipment ID namespaces remain separate (existing platform guarantee).

result.routes[].steps[].id.description: Member ID (technician ID). Each member appears as an ordinary job step in a vehicle route.

result.routes[].steps[].coordination_gro.description: Coordination group ID. Links this step to its group for synchronization verification.

result.routes[].steps[].arrival.description: Arrival time at location (seconds since epoch). Raw arrival; not necessarily synchronized. Use waiting_time to compute service_start.

result.routes[].steps[].waiting_time.description: Waiting time (seconds) before service starts. Includes time-window wait + coordination wait (wait for other members to arrive). service_start = arrival + waiting_time.

result.routes[].steps[].service.description: Actual service duration (seconds) applied to this member.

result.unassigned.description: If any member of a group is infeasible, all members appear in unassigned[] with reason explaining the blockage (e.g., 'insufficient vehicles', 'arrival_sync tolerance exceeded', 'time window infeasible').

testingSuggestions: Positive: Basic 2-member group (electrician + HVAC), different vehicles, same location, arrival within 5 min tolerance.
Positive: 3-member group, 3 distinct vehicles, all within tolerance.
Positive: Verify coordination_group_id populated on all members.
Positive: Verify members on different vehicles (vehicle(member1) != vehicle(member2)).
Positive: Verify same location for all members.
Positive: Verify arrival spread <= tolerance: abs(arrival_A - arrival_B) <= tolerance. Note: Check service_start sync, not raw arrival.
Positive: Different service durations: electrician 3600s, HVAC 1800s → both have same service_start under last_arrival, different finish times.
Positive: last_arrival (default): both members start service at same time (latest arrival).
Positive: first_arrival: each member starts service on own arrival; departures differ.
Positive: Group skills + member skills: group [7], member [20] → vehicle needs {7,20}.
Positive: No group-level load; each member's load independent.
Positive: Pinned member: force technician to specific vehicle using relations.
Positive: Multiple groups in one request: group 501 & group 777 coordinate independently; same vehicle can appear in both at different times.
Negative-validation: Fast API + coordinate_jobs → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: 1 member (min 2) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Missing group ID → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Missing location_index → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Duplicate group ID → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Member ID matches normal job ID → HTTP 400 (global uniqueness).
Negative-validation: Same vehicle pinned to two members of same group → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Invalid arrival_sync_tolerance_seconds (negative or > 86400) → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Invalid service_start_rule (not 'last_arrival' or 'first_arrival') → HTTP 400.
Negative-infeasible: Only 1 eligible vehicle (not enough for 2+ members) → entire group UNASSIGNED.
Negative-infeasible: Arrival spread > tolerance (e.g. 20 min with 5 min tolerance) → entire group UNASSIGNED.
Negative-infeasible: Non-overlapping member time windows → entire group UNASSIGNED.
Negative-infeasible: Member time window that cannot fit service duration → entire group UNASSIGNED.
Boundary: Arrival exactly at tolerance boundary → assigned.
Boundary: Arrival 1 second beyond tolerance → unassigned.
Boundary: arrival_sync_tolerance_seconds=0 (requires exact synchronization) → assigned only if shared time window forces identical arrivals.
Interaction: Skills test: group [7], members [20],[21] → vehicle_A needs {7,20}, vehicle_B needs {7,21}.
Interaction: Missing vehicle with group skill: group [7], member with [20], but no vehicle has both → entire group UNASSIGNED.
Interaction: Pinned + different vehicles: pin member A to vehicle X, member B to vehicle Y → both assigned (X!=Y maintained).
Interaction: Two members pinned to same vehicle → HTTP 400.
Interaction: Member pinned in non-coordinate context → HTTP 400.
Interaction: Re-optimization: remove group by ID → all members removed (not partial).
Backward compatibility: Requests without coordinate_jobs pass through unchanged; all coordinates-less tests must regress clean.
limitations: Flexible API only. Fast API (jsprit) returns HTTP 400 if coordinate_jobs is present.
Shipment members not supported. Members are job-type visits only (not pickup+delivery pairs).
Nested coordination groups not supported. Groups cannot contain other groups.
Simulation mode not supported in v1.
Live hold/re-plan not supported. If technician is late in real life, re-optimize with updated inputs (no in-mission synchronization).
Time-window inheritance: member time_windows fully replaces group (not intersection). If member specifies windows, group windows ignored entirely.
Multi-window blind spot: if member A can reach its early window but member B cannot, A takes early window, spread check fails, group rejected. Planned for v2 coupled search.

No explicit meeting-window selection objective. Window is anchored at max(window intersections, earliest reachable), with randomized offsets (≤ 4 hours) across iterations; final plan selected by standard cost criteria.
No meeting-time persistence across re-optimization. If group re-planned, window re-chosen from scratch (not seeded from prior arrivals).
Synchronization asserted on service_start (arrival + waiting), not raw arrival. Raw arrivals can differ widely (up to 4+ hours) even with tolerance=300 if shared time window aligns them.

features.title: Multi-Order Merging (Metric-Driven Same-Location Job Grouping)
features.description: Enable metric-driven merging of co-located jobs into multi-order stops, where the optimizer decides which same-location orders to combine based on plan quality. Solves the Velocitor use case: backend no longer needs to pre-merge orders (which loses information), and the optimizer merges only where it improves the solution. Also removes the restriction that a job may carry only pickup OR delivery (now allows both). Two sub-features: (1) mixed pickup+delivery per job (§2.1, unconditional), and (2) multi-order merging (§2.2, opt-in, defaults to off).

multiorders.description: Multi-order grouping configuration (DRAFT, not in spec): opt-in metric-driven merging of co-located jobs. Flexible API only; Fast API returns 400 if present.

merge.description: Enable metric-driven multi-order merging. When true, optimizer combines co-located eligible orders only where the combination improves the plan (total objective). Default: false.

force_merge.description: Force merging of every eligible co-located group, regardless of plan quality. Requires merge=true. Warning: may worsen planning results; use only if orders at same address are significantly smaller than vehicle capacity. Default: false.

radius_m.description: Proximity radius for treating nearby orders as one address (in meters). NOT SUPPORTED in v1; must be 0. Only exact location_index match is used for grouping. Default: 0.

can_be_merged.description: Per-order opt-out from multi-order merging. When false, this job is never merged with co-located jobs, even if merging is enabled. Default: true. Lives on jobs[].properties (not nested under multiorders).
can_be_merged.note: This is a job-level field, not under options.multiorders; include in jobs.items.properties.

constraints: Flexible API only. Fast API requests with options.multiorders present return HTTP 400.

§2.1: Mixed pickup+delivery validation removed. A job may now carry both pickup and delivery quantities simultaneously. Capacity is checked separately for each direction (never netted). These three combinations remain rejected: (a) follow_lifo_order with both quantities, (b) depot_ids with both quantities, (c) split.can_be_split with both quantities.
§2.2.2: Three parameters group under options.multiorders: merge, force_merge, radius_m.
merge=true enables metric-driven merging; false disables it (default). When disabled, co-located jobs are planned as separate stops, exactly as today.
force_merge requires merge=true; submit with force_merge=true and merge=false/absent returns HTTP 400.
radius_m must be 0 (only value supported). Any positive value returns HTTP 400. Keep field for request-shape stability; radius-based proximity is future work (§Out of scope).

§2.4: Eligibility criteria for multi-order candidacy (hard admissibility rules, not negotiable): (a) Same location_index (necessary key), (b) can_be_merged=true on all jobs, (c) Identical skills, (d) Identical zones, (e) Non-empty time_window intersection, (f) load_types/incompatible_load_types sets must not conflict, (g) sequence_order must match or absent on both, (h) joint_order must match or absent on both, (i) depot_ids must be identical AND merge must not produce both quantities, (j) split.can_be_split must be false, (k) follow_lifo_order must be false, (l) volume (3D packing) must be absent, (m) max_time_in_vehicle must be absent.
Eligibility partitions jobs at a location into candidate groups + ineligible jobs (no error; ineligible jobs planned separately).

§2.3: After eligibility, optimizer decides whether each candidate should be realized as a multi-order. Decision happens during search, not preprocessing. Candidate is formed only where the total objective improves. Per-order costs (costs.per_order, unassigned penalty) are counted on original orders, not the merged stop, to prevent bias toward merging.

force_merge=true overrides this decision and forms every candidate unconditionally. Dissolve move is disabled. Warning: a multi-order that no vehicle can absorb gets unassigned with all its member orders unassigned (all-or-nothing).

§2.5: Aggregation rules for merged-stop values: service=sum, setup=max, delivery/pickup=dimension-wise sum (never netted), time_windows=intersection, priority=max, revenue/outsourcing_cost=sum, max_visit_lateness=min, description=joined ('; '-separated).

§2.6: Response representation. A realized multi-order produces one job-type step with: (a) step.id = synthetic multi-order id (reserved high numeric range, never appears in request), (b) step.original_job_ids = ascending array of merged job ids (new field, present only on multi-order steps), (c) step.service/setup/delivery/pickup aggregated per §2.5, (d) step.load = post-stop load (load_before - delivery + pickup).
Unassigned[] reports orders individually under original ids; multi-order id never appears in unassigned[].
Summary counters (total jobs, pickup, delivery) count original orders, never multi-order stops.

§2.7: Multi-order ids are ephemeral (per-plan only, not durable keys). Same address can merge in one plan and stay separate in the next as inputs change. Consumers must key off original_job_ids, never multi-order ids.
Multi-order ids come from reserved high numeric range; submitting a job id in that range is a 400 error.
Ids are assigned deterministically, so same request + same seed = same ids.
No string multi-order id; API returns numeric only. MVRO composes customer-facing label from original_job_ids.

§3.3: Re-optimization uses original job ids in input (multi-order ids rejected at validation). Previous plan's groupings recovered from shared step; same grouping remains stable if inputs unchanged. If changes make a merge a bad idea, dissolve move applies and multi-orders break up. Ids reassigned for new plan (invisible if consumer reads original_job_ids).
Shipments are never merged in v1; only jobs. A shipment step and co-located job stay separate.
Candidate merging is single-plan (optimizer weighs each candidate against plan being built, not exhaustive merge-combination search).

routes.steps.original_job_ids.description: New field. Array of original job ids that were merged into this multi-order step, in ascending order. Present only on multi-order steps. Absent on ordinary steps (job_id only). Used by MVRO to fan-out multi-order result back to original orders.
routes.steps.original_job_ids.note: Use presence of this field to distinguish multi-order step from ordinary step (more robust than type-flag approach).

routes.steps.service.description: Multi-order value: sum(service) over merged orders. Existing field; semantics widened.

routes.steps.setup.description: Multi-order value: max(setup) over merged orders. Existing field; semantics widened.

routes.steps.delivery.description: Multi-order value: dimension-wise sum of delivery quantities over merged orders. Existing field; now populated for multi-order steps (previously only for split jobs).

routes.steps.pickup.description: Multi-order value: dimension-wise sum of pickup quantities over merged orders. Existing field; now populated for multi-order steps (previously only for split jobs).

routes.steps.load.description: Post-stop load: load_before - delivery + pickup. Existing field; applies to multi-order steps.

result.unassigned.description: If a multi-order merge candidate cannot be served (combined load exceeds all vehicles, or some other block), individual orders are reported in unassigned[] under their own ids. Reason string may mention grouping context where multiple orders of same candidate are unassigned together.

testingSuggestions: Positive-feature-parity: Mixed pickup+delivery (no merging): one job with delivery=6, pickup=4, vehicle capacity=10 → assigned; vehicle leaves depot with 6, carries 4 after stop, routes show both pickup and delivery.
Positive-feature-parity: Mixed pickup+delivery (no merging), capacity check on peak: same job, vehicle capacity=5 → unassigned (need 6 for delivery peak, not netted to 2).
Positive: Merging off (default): two co-located jobs (3min service, 2min service) with merge=false/absent → two separate steps at same location under own ids, second starts after first finishes.
Positive: Merging on, improves plan: same two small jobs, merge=true → one multi-order step, 5 min total service, setup counted once, original_job_ids=[id1, id2], combined delivery/pickup populated.

Positive: Merging on, does not improve: three co-located orders whose combined load exceeds every vehicle, but fit as 2-vehicle solution → not merged; all three on separate steps under own ids, both vehicles used, no unassigned order.
Positive: Merging on, eligibility partition: three co-located jobs, one requires extra skill → skilled job never a candidate; other two may merge. No error.
Positive: Merging on, time-window intersection: orders promised 09:00-10:00 and 09:30-11:00 → candidates; if merged, stop must arrive in 09:30-10:00.
Positive: Merging on, disjoint time windows: orders promised 09:00-09:30 and 10:00-11:00 → never candidates; always separate steps.

Positive: Forced merging shows trade-off: three co-located orders with combined load exceeding all vehicles, force_merge=true → merged into one multi-order that no vehicle absorbs; all three members unassigned with group-context reason.
Positive: force_merge requires merge: force_merge=true with merge=false/absent → HTTP 400.
Positive: Per-order opt-out: three co-located small orders, one with can_be_merged=false → at most two-member multi-order plus one separate step.
Positive: Original job ids preserved: multi-order with id=999 from merge of [id1=117, id2=118] → original_job_ids=[117,118], ascending order.
Positive: Deterministic ids: same request + same seed → same multi-order ids in result.
Positive: Verify multi-order step fields: service=sum, setup=max, delivery/pickup=dimension-wise sums, load computed correctly.
Positive: Verify response consistency: step.service + step.setup = total time at stop (matches RouteQ formula).
Positive: Verify per-member timing: all members start service at same time under last_arrival (default).
Positive: Verify unassigned reporting: unassigned members reported individually under own ids (not multi-order id).
Positive: Multi-dimensional amounts: two orders [300,15] and [100,5] merged → multi-order delivery/pickup are [400,20].
Positive: Verify load progression: start 0 → before merged stop X → after merged stop (X-delivery+pickup) → end.
Positive: Re-optimization stability: re-run same request → same grouping intact; remove one order → grouping dissolves (remaining order separate).
Positive: Re-optimization input correction: previous plan had multi-order id, re-opt uses original_job_ids → accepted; multi-order id in re-opt input → rejected.
Negative-validation: radius_m set to any value != 0 → HTTP 400 (not supported in v1).
Negative-validation: force_merge=true without merge=true → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Job id in reserved multi-order range → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Re-optimization with multi-order id in input → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Relation referencing multi-order id → HTTP 400 (relations must reference original job ids).
Negative-validation: Mixed pickup+delivery with follow_lifo_order → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Mixed pickup+delivery with depot_ids → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Mixed pickup+delivery with split.can_be_split → HTTP 400.
Negative-validation: Fast API with options.multiorders present → HTTP 400.
Negative-infeasible: Merging attempt, no vehicle can serve combined load → both orders unassigned.
Boundary: merge=true, force_merge=false (recommended): optimizer chooses per-candidate; some addresses merge, others don't as plan evolves.
Boundary: merge=true, force_merge=true (warning): all candidates forced; may produce unassigned multi-orders.
Boundary: Arrival exactly at eligibility threshold → included in candidate.
Boundary: Arrival 1 sec outside time-window intersection → not a candidate.
Interaction: Skills + zones: orders eligible if skills identical AND zones identical (both conditions required).
Interaction: Priority in merged stop: max(priority) → single-priority group; priority serves as rank, summing would be wrong.
Interaction: LIFO constraint: LIFO-ordered job can never merge (eligibility rule). If you need LIFO + merging, split into separate locations (workaround).
Interaction: Pinned vehicle: relations with type=pinned can restrict where merged members go. If pin restricts members to different vehicles, merge cannot occur.
Backward-compatibility: Existing requests without multiorders options pass unchanged. All non-merging tests regress clean. Mixed pickup+delivery only active if explicitly sent.
limitations: radius_m not supported. Only exact location_index match defines co-location. Customers with per-order geocoding must deduplicate addresses themselves. Radius-based proximity is top item of §Out of scope.
Merging is not guaranteed. It is an optimizer decision, so enabling merge=true does not promise one stop per address. Same address may merge in one plan and not in the next as inputs change.
Multi-order ids are per-plan, not durable. Must never be stored as keys. If consumer caches id as stable reference, re-optimization will break the mapping. Use original_job_ids.
Time-window intersection is conservative. Disjoint windows → never candidates, even where vehicle could serve in two visits.
Not eligible to merge: split orders, LIFO-ordered jobs, 3D volume jobs, jobs with max_time_in_vehicle, jobs with per-job depot bindings producing both quantities.
Shipments not merged in v1. A shipment step and co-located job stay separate steps.
Merging decided within one plan. Optimizer weights each candidate against plan being built, not against exhaustive search over every merge combination.
Excluded from simulation mode (simulation-mode.md).
§2.1 (mixed pickup+delivery) carries none of the above limitations. It is unconditional and independent of multi-order options.

features.title: Multi-Order: jobs[].can_be_merged (Per-Order Opt-Out)
features.description: Per-order opt-out from multi-order merging (companion to multi-order-v2). When can_be_merged=false on a job, that job is excluded from every multi-order grouping, even if options.multiorders.merge=true. Lives directly on the job object (jobs[].can_be_merged). Keeps RouteQ's field name and default (true).

can_be_merged.description: Per-order opt-out from multi-order merging. When false, this job is never merged with co-located jobs, even if options.multiorders.merge=true. When true (default), job is eligible for merging subject to eligibility rules (§2.4 of Multi_Order_V2.pdf).

constraints: Only meaningful when options.multiorders.merge=true. If merging is disabled globally, this field is ignored.
When can_be_merged=false, the job is planned as a standalone stop (never grouped with co-located jobs).
This is a per-order field; different jobs at the same location can have different can_be_merged values, partitioning eligible and ineligible groups.
Eligible jobs with can_be_merged=false are never candidates for merging; ineligible jobs are never candidates regardless of this field (eligibility rules in §2.4 take precedence).
Flexible API only; Fast API silently ignores this field.
testingSuggestions: Positive: Merging off (default, merge absent/false): can_be_merged value ignored; all jobs standalone regardless of field value.
Positive: Merging on, can_be_merged=true (default): job eligible for grouping with co-located orders (subject to §2.4 eligibility rules).
Positive: Merging on, can_be_merged=false: job planned standalone; co-located jobs with can_be_merged=true may still merge with each other.
Positive: Three co-located jobs, one with can_be_merged=false → at most two-job multi-order step + one separate step under the opt-out job's id.
Positive: Verify can_be_merged=false job appears as ordinary job step (not in multi-order).
Positive: Multiple jobs with can_be_merged=false at same location → each stays separate (no merging among them either).
Negative-validation: Non-boolean can_be_merged (e.g., string 'false') → HTTP 400 validation error.
limitations: Only affects multi-order eligibility. Does not prevent a job from being combined via other mechanisms.
Field value is evaluated per-request; no persistence across re-optimization. Each re-optimization re-evaluates can_be_merged afresh.
